title: Fix: Rename misnamed linker script in STM32F401RE-Nucleo Template
author: Jorgeto0
body:
## Problem
The linker script was incorrectly named STM32F401CEUX_FLASH.ld which references the F401CE chip variant in UFQFPN48 package.

The Nucleo-F401RE board uses the STM32F401RET6 chip (LQFP64 package), so the linker script should be named STM32F401RETX_FLASH.ld to match STM32CubeIDE's auto-generated convention.

**Changes made:**
- Renamed STM32F401CEUX_FLASH.ld → STM32F401RETX_FLASH.ld
- Updated linker script header from F401CEUx to F401RETx
- Updated all 4 filename references in .cproject file
- Updated chip name references in .cproject from F401CEUx to F401RETx

This aligns the Template with what STM32CubeIDE actually generates and prevents confusion for developers using this template.

**Verification:**
- The Nucleo-F401RE board uses the STM32F401RET6 chip as confirmed in [UM1724 Table 1](https://www.st.com/resource/en/user_manual/um1724-stm32-nucleo64-boards-mb1136-stmicroelectronics.pdf)
- STM32CubeIDE auto-generates STM32F401RETX_FLASH.ld for this board as shown in [this example](https://github.com/parikshitpagare/digital-clock-rtc/blob/main/STM32F401RETX_FLASH.ld)

title: Fix: Rename misnamed linker script in STM32F401RE-Nucleo Template
author: Jorgeto0
body:
## Problem

The STM32F401RE-Nucleo Templates folder contains a linker script with an incorrect filename and chip references that do not match the actual hardware on the board.

## Issue Details

The Nucleo-F401RE board uses the STM32F401RET6 microcontroller (64-pin LQFP package). However, the template linker script was incorrectly named for the STM32F401CEUx variant (48-pin UFQFPN package). This creates confusion for developers using the template, as:

- The board uses **STM32F401RET6** (LQFP64 package, "T" suffix)
- The template referenced **STM32F401CEUx** (UFQFPN48 package, "U" suffix)
- STM32CubeIDE auto-generates `STM32F401RETX_FLASH.ld` for this board
- The naming inconsistency could lead developers to question whether they are using the correct template

## Changes Made

- Renamed `STM32F401CEUX_FLASH.ld` to `STM32F401RETX_FLASH.ld`
- Updated linker script header comment from `F401CEUx` to `F401RETx`
- Updated all filename references in the `.cproject` file
- Updated chip variant references in `.cproject` from `STM32F401CEUx` to `STM32F401RETx`

## Impact

- Template now matches STM32CubeIDE's auto-generated naming convention
- Eliminates confusion about which chip variant the template targets
- Correctly reflects the actual hardware on the Nucleo-F401RE board

## Verification

**Board Hardware:**
- Confirmed Nucleo-F401RE uses STM32F401RET6 per [UM1724 User Manual, Table 1](https://www.st.com/resource/en/user_manual/um1724-stm32-nucleo64-boards-mb1136-stmicroelectronics.pdf)

**STM32CubeIDE Generated Naming:**
- Verified through multiple open-source projects showing auto-generated linker scripts:
  - [parikshitpagare/digital-clock-rtc](https://github.com/parikshitpagare/digital-clock-rtc/blob/main/STM32F401RETX_FLASH.ld)
  - [lamik/EEPROM-emulation-STM32F4-HAL](https://github.com/lamik/EEPROM-emulation-STM32F4-HAL/blob/master/STM32F401RETX_FLASH.ld)

title: prevent memory corruption
author: maggu2810
body:
An USB device that provides more endpoints then the defined maximum supported ones of the code base this will lead to a memory corruption.
The code does not check if it runs over the maximum defined endpoints and write to the memory behind of it.
For the number of interfaces the check if the maximum is already reached is present, for the endpoints it is missing.

title: [ETH] Fixed errors in bit positions
author: DedkovArtem
body:
fixed multiple errors in bit positions in registers.

In version 1.26.2, the structure fields were assigned values already taking into account the bit position in the register. 
For example
`macinit.ZeroQuantaPause = ETH_ZEROQUANTAPAUSE_DISABLE;`
where
`#define ETH_ZEROQUANTAPAUSE_DISABLE 0x00000080U`

in version 1.27.0, some fields of the structure are assigned the values 1 or 0. And when these fields are written to the register, the offset by the bit position is not taken into account.
For example
`macDefaultConf.ZeroQuantaPause = DISABLE;`
where
`DISABLE=0U`

title: Add ability to redefine VECT_TAB_OFFSET by user (system_stm32f4xx.c)
author: DenDeg
body:
Unlike HSE_VALUE or HSI_VALUE,  VECT_TAB_OFFSET value defined in _STM32CubeF4/Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32F4xx/Source/Templates/system_stm32f4xx.c_ can't be redefined by user. Some building scripts (like Platformio ststm32 platform with stm32cube framework script) and libs depends on default _system_stm32f4xx.c_, so I can't just create my own _system_stm32f4xx.c_ file. This becomes a problem when writing firmware that uses a bootloader, because there's no way to change VECT_TAB_OFFSET without modifying default file.
Suggested small code change adds ability to redefine VECT_TAB_OFFSET by user.

title: Whitespace and character set housekeeping
author: tcv-git
body:
This pull-request makes no functional changes.  It only:

1.  Strips trailing white space from the end of lines in driver source files.

2. Converts the character set of driver source files to ASCII.  Some were previously Windows-1252, and some were UTF-8.  Note that this only affects special characters (curly quotes etc) in comments, not code.

3.  Expands tabs to spaces in driver source files.  In different files tabs are expanded to 2, 4 or 8 spaces.  Most indentation was already in spaces.  This makes it possible to determine the correct number of spaces that the original author intended and to make the files look consistent whatever the editor setting.

title: Set HAL_UART_STATE_READY at end of UART_DMATransmitCplt()
author: milesfrain
body:
Calling `HAL_UART_Transmit_DMA()` will set `huart->gState = HAL_UART_STATE_BUSY_TX;`. But then `gState` is never reset to `HAL_UART_STATE_READY`, so you cannot successfully call this function again to make another DMA transfer in the future.
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/5d01400afd60410f6e049cbd19179a67d44d53fd/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_uart.c#L1297-L1317

One workaround is to call `HAL_UART_Init()` to reset `gState` before each call to `HAL_UART_Transmit_DMA()`, but I don't think this is the suggested usage.

Not sure if I'm simply misusing the library, and / or if this proposed change is the best fix.

title: Set HAL_UART_STATE_READY at end of UART_DMAReceiveCplt()
author: milesfrain
body:
Calling `HAL_UART_Transmit_DMA()` will set `huart->gState = HAL_UART_STATE_BUSY_TX;`. But then `gState` is never reset to `HAL_UART_STATE_READY`, so you cannot successfully call this function again to make another DMA transfer in the future.
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/5d01400afd60410f6e049cbd19179a67d44d53fd/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_uart.c#L1297-L1317

One workaround is to call `HAL_UART_Init()` to reset `gState` before each call to `HAL_UART_Transmit_DMA()`, but I don't think this is the suggested usage.

Not sure if this fix is the best option.

title: fix IS_ADC_CHANNEL() bug on STM32F411xE variants
author: TheCodeSharman
body:
This PR fixes an issue where the following is returning false for the STM32F411xE chip: 

`IS_ADC_CHANNEL(ADC_CHANNEL_TEMPSENSOR) `

As a result of this the [example code on the Wiki](https://github.com/stm32duino/wiki/wiki/API#example-2) for reading the internal temperature sensor returns a result of -266 because analogRead(ATEMP) always returns 0 indicating an error.

Note: Reviewing the code it looks like the definition of ADC_CHANNEL_TEMPSENSOR is inconsistent with the definition of IS_ADC_CHANNEL for other boards too? I've only made the minimal changes for the board I own however.
